messages:
Kai (Design): quick UX thread: we're reworking the Pools 'mass prune' flow. two related questions: required-field affordance (asterisk vs full "Required" label) and how to surface failures when many rows error during a mass operation. want low noise + predictable keyboard + clear copy for destructive confirms. Maya (PM): for mass ops, summarize failures up top. users expect a single status area. but we should offer inline context for the first few failures. Tess (Eng): agree on summary-first. implementation note: summary should include per-error jump links that expand the row inline rather than navigate away. keep DOM stable to avoid layout shift. Zoe (DevEx): keyboard flow: after submit failure, focus should land on the summary container. first Tab should go to first anchor. ESC closes expanded row and returns focus to its anchor. I'll add this to keyboard acceptance. Kai (Design): for required indicators, i'm pushing a compromise: explicit "Required" label for primary inputs (name, owner) and a visually subtle asterisk for others. but the asterisk needs an accessible legend up top. a11y-bot: suggestion: if using mixed signals, include a single visually-hidden explanation for the pattern and ensure both markers are exposed to AT. Example:
Fields marked "Required" or * are mandatory.
Also recommend visible text for important fields for clarity. Maya (PM): makes sense. keep visible 'Required' only where product-critical, otherwise asterisk. document pattern in the component spec. Tess (Eng): back to errors: propose a hybrid: top summary (aria-live, focus moved there) listing counts + quick filters (permissions, locked, in-use), then inline collapsed details for the first 3 failures which expand in place. anchors should have aria-controls to reveal region. Kai (Design): nice. i'd also like to try showing a small inline breadcrumb to help users trace which selection caused the error (eg., "Selected by tag: analytics-team"). helps when list came from a filter. Zoe (DevEx): acceptance criteria: 1) focus on summary after submit, 2) Tab lands on first anchor, 3) activating anchor expands inline region and moves focus to its header, 4) ESC collapses and returns focus to anchor. I'll add tests. Tess (Eng): typed-confirm debate: full typed name vs checkbox vs "type to enable" pattern. i'm leaning toward a conditional typed-confirm for org-owned or high-impact pools. alternatives: short delay (+disabled CTA for 2s) to avoid instant accidents. Maya (PM): conditional typed-confirm sounds right. prefer allowing admins to flip the behavior in settings. also open to a small countdown on the CTA for extra caution on very large deletes. Kai (Design): copy suggestion: instead of bland "Type name to confirm" try: "Enter the exact pool name to permanently remove it." and show a small line: "This cannot be undone." If countdown is used, show it in the CTA: "Delete (3s)". a11y-bot: accessibility notes for typed-confirm: autofocus the input, set autocomplete="off", use aria-invalid when mismatch, and tie aria-describedby to helper text. If using countdown, ensure timer updates are announced via aria-live only at sensible intervals to avoid noise. Also allow paste and exact-match rules should be explicit (trim whitespace; recommend case-sensitive unless PM requests otherwise). Maya (PM): decision proposal: 1) Required marker: explicit 'Required' for key fields, asterisk for others with legend. 2) Error surface: hybrid summary-first (aria-live focus) + inline collapsed details for first 3 failures; anchors expand inline with aria-controls. 3) Typed-confirm: opt-in for org-owned/high-impact pools; allow admin override; if enabled, autofocus, disable CTA until trimmed exact match, allow paste; optionally support a short CTA countdown for very large operations. 4) Microcopy: use 'permanently remove/ permanently delete' phrasing and an undo note only if undo exists. Tess (Eng): ack. i'll file tickets for focus movement, anchor expand behavior, and the optional countdown impl. Zoe (DevEx): i'll add keyboard/a11y checks to the PR template and draft a quick manual test. Kai (Design): i'll push mocks for the hybrid summary + inline preview and the confirm modal with countdown variants. tagging @Tess @Zoe @Maya for review. Maya (PM): thanks all, updating the product doc with the conditional rules and rollout guidance.
